item: A pass-tail thread that cannot be started (briefing refresh, housekeeping lane) frees its non-overlap lock instead of holding it for the life of the process
refs: found by the read of #1629; PR pending
summary: _refresh_briefing_async and _kick_housekeeping_lane took a non-blocking lock, built a thread whose _run releases it in a finally, and called Thread.start(); start() raises RuntimeError (can't start new thread) before the target runs, so the finally never ran: every later pass skipped the launch as still running and whole_corpus_work_running read true until the process ended. A new _start_detached logs the failure at WARNING, releases the lock only when the thread never got an ident (a thread that did run releases for itself; releasing twice would raise) and lets the pass go on. Six tests, all red on the unchanged runner; release-unconditionally and no-release mutants red.
